Why is there a tiny hole in almost every airplane window? It isn't a flaw. It is keeping that window in one piece. A plane window has three panes. The outer pane is the strong one. The middle pane is the backup, and it has the hole. At cruising altitude, the cabin holds far more air pressure than the thin air outside, so the window is constantly being pushed outward. The hole lets cabin air into the gap between the panes, so the outer pane takes the load and the middle one stays ready. It also helps keep the window from fogging up.
